clue.text: One defending terse announcement of 1997 election result?

definitions.meaning: a defender on the left side of a football team
in 1997 Labour returned to power, so a two-word headline might say the political left is back in government

explanation.surface: A clipped news flash about Labour's 1997 landslide, delivered by a defender.
explanation.walkthrough: A double definition. The 1997 UK general election brought Labour, the party of the left, back into government after eighteen years.
explanation.definitionFit: A full back playing on the left flank is a defender, matching one who defends.

clue.text: Newspaper story involving sex, vice and lust? No way

indicators.note: involving here means tangling together, so the letters are intricately rearranged
No tells us to take the letters for way out of the word lust

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way

explanation.surface: A tabloid scoop full of sex, vice and lust, dismissed with a scornful 'No way'.
explanation.walkthrough: 'No way' removes ST from LUST, leaving LU; 'involving' then rearranges SEX + VICE + LU into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A scoop printed by only one paper is called an exclusive, a newspaper story no rival has.

clue.text: Minute, it eats into tree destructively

definitions.text: Minute, it eats into tree destructively

indicators.note: eats into means one piece burrows inside another, here the minute letter going in
destructively signals that the letters of it and tree are wrecked and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A tiny pest boring into timber and wrecking it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'destructively' makes TERITE, which 'eats into' opens to take M. Read whole, the clue also describes what the insect does to wood.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue pictures the tiny insect that bores into wood and destroys it.

clue.text: Take leisurely stroll, being fit to cover miles

indicators.note: to cover means to wrap around, so the word for fit goes outside the letter for miles

parts.note: fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: Someone fit enough could walk miles at an easy pace.
explanation.definitionFit: To amble is to walk at a slow, relaxed pace, a leisurely stroll.

clue.text: Flyer issued by takeaway

indicators.note: issued by suggests letters coming out of the word takeaway, which contains them

explanation.surface: A leaflet put out by a fast-food takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The kea is a New Zealand parrot; 'Flyer' looks like a leaflet but means a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A kea is a mountain parrot of New Zealand, so it is a bird that flies.

clue.text: I may be embraced by lover at church

definitions.text: I may be embraced by lover at church

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so the letter I goes within the word for lover

parts.note: a fan is a lover or devotee of something
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A betrothed person anticipating a hug from their partner at the wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be embraced by' makes FIAN. Read whole, the clue describes someone engaged, greeted by a partner at the church wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: A betrothed man is the one his lover may embrace at the church wedding.

clue.text: Visor, a means of preserving one's dignity

definitions.meaning: a visor protects the face, playfully something that saves one's face

definitions.text: a means of preserving one's dignity
definitions.meaning: something that lets one avoid humiliation or keep up appearances

explanation.surface: A visor described as the thing that keeps one dignified.
explanation.walkthrough: A double definition; the first is a playful literal reading of a guard that protects the face.
explanation.definitionFit: A compromise that avoids humiliation is called by this name, preserving one's dignity.

clue.text: Writer is featured in supplement

indicators.note: featured in means placed within, so is goes inside the word for supplement

parts.note: an add-on is an extra or supplement

explanation.surface: A writer appearing in a newspaper's weekend supplement.
explanation.walkthrough: Joseph Addison was an English essayist, co-founder of The Spectator.
explanation.definitionFit: Joseph Addison was an eighteenth-century English essayist, poet and playwright.

clue.text: Collection of writing with chapte by author unknown

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for chapter, the word the paper prints without its final letter
anon, short for anonymous, marks a work whose author is unknown

explanation.surface: An anthology containing a chapter by an anonymous writer.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is the accepted body of works by a writer or of a literature, a collection.

clue.text: Tree expert's right

parts.note: an ace is an expert; the 's stands for has, a link

explanation.surface: A tree specialist claiming to be correct.
explanation.walkthrough: Acer is the botanical name of the maple genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the genus of maples, so an acer is a tree.

clue.text: With wacky baccy, I make impression that's not intended

indicators.note: wacky means crazy, so the letters of baccy and I are jumbled

parts.note: a dent is an impression made in a surface

explanation.surface: Someone smoking odd tobacco leaves a mark they never meant to make.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wacky' makes BYACCI. Baccy is British slang for tobacco, so the surface suggests a strange smoke.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done unintentionally happens by chance rather than by design.

clue.text: Functions held by public transport companies

indicators.note: held by means contained within, so the word for functions sits inside the public transport

parts.note: buses are a form of public transport
sines are trigonometric functions

explanation.surface: Corporate functions hosted aboard public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Functions' suggests social events, but here it means trigonometric functions; 'held by' splits the transport word after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Businesses are commercial firms, so they are companies.

clue.text: Holidaying briefly in island state

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the shortened word goes within the island

parts.note: Sark is one of the Channel Islands

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: someone holidaying is away

explanation.surface: Taking a short break on an island state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' leaves AWA; 'in' places it inside a small Channel Island. 'island state' tempts as one definition, but the answer is a Malaysian state on Borneo.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarawak is a state of Malaysia on the island of Borneo.

clue.text: Confess crime to avoid "time"

indicators.note: to avoid means to leave out, so the letter for time is dropped

parts.note: a sting is a swindle or confidence trick

explanation.surface: A criminal owning up to dodge a prison sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' looks like a jail term but is just T; to sing is slang for informing to the police.
explanation.definitionFit: In criminal slang to sing is to inform or confess to the police.

clue.text: Terrible performer missing entrance, answerable to him?

parts.note: dire means terrible

indicators.note: missing entrance means without its first letter, the way in

parts.note: an actor is a performer

explanation.surface: A bad actor who misses his cue, accountable to the person in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entrance' suggests a stage entry but means the first letter. The definition is cryptic: the performer is answerable to the person running the show.
explanation.definitionFit: Actors answer to the person who directs the production, so the definition describes that role.

clue.text: Device in cab shows extra time erroneously

indicators.note: erroneously means wrongly, so the letters of extra time are set out in a new order

explanation.surface: A taxi meter charging for extra time by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A taximeter is the instrument in a cab that calculates the fare.

clue.text: Go like a delivery vehicle?

parts.note: read as van plus -ish, like a van; also to go means to disappear

explanation.surface: Moving in the manner of a delivery van.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish is to go, disappear from sight; the clue also splits it as van-like.

clue.text: Cold wearing knitted garment? Jacket needed

indicators.note: wearing means having on, so the garment goes round the letter for cold

parts.note: a slipover is a sleeveless knitted pullover

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold wearing a jumper still needs a jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: A slipcover is a removable cover for furniture or a book, so 'Jacket' as a dust jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: A slipcover is a protective cover, such as a book's dust jacket.

clue.text: Automatic response on approaching bend

indicators.note: approaching means coming just before, so the first piece sits next to the second

parts.note: re means on, concerning
to flex is to bend

explanation.surface: A driver reacting instinctively as a bend comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex is an involuntary automatic reaction of the body.

clue.text: Crucial matches unable to start: because of these?

indicators.note: unable to start means losing the first letter

parts.note: play-offs are deciding matches in a competition

explanation.surface: Important games cannot begin because players have been laid off.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: workers are unable to start work because of redundancies.
explanation.definitionFit: Layoffs are dismissals of workers, the reason people cannot start their jobs.

clue.text: Campaign to eliminate last of mice at home, using rodent poison

indicators.note: to eliminate means to remove, so the letter chosen is taken out

parts.note: warfare is a military campaign

indicators.note: last of means the final letter of the word mice

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A pest control drive to wipe out mice in the house with poison.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfarin is an anticoagulant used as a poison to kill rats and mice.

clue.text: Being discussed perhaps out loud hay-fever sufferer may interject this

indicators.note: out loud means spoken, so the words are heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a matter being discussed is at issue

explanation.surface: A sneeze cutting into a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' is a link. AT ISSUE spoken quickly sounds like the sneeze.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the conventional written sound of a sneeze, which a hay-fever sufferer may let out.

clue.text: Tense editor's long day finishes

parts.note: ED is the abbreviation for editor; the 's is a link

indicators.note: finishes means the final letters of long and day

explanation.surface: A stressed editor at the end of a long day.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgy means nervous or tense.

clue.text: Woman brings up an excellent daughter

indicators.note: in a down clue brings up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-class or excellent, written AI

explanation.surface: A woman raising a fine daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings up' reverses AN + AI + D, giving the woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana is a woman's first name.

clue.text: Bid for contract to supply part of new stadium?

definitions.meaning: to try to win business by presenting an offer
literally to construct a playing field, a sports pitch

explanation.surface: A tender to provide the playing surface of a new stadium.
explanation.definitionFit: To make a pitch is to make a sales bid; literally it builds a sports field.

clue.text: From what we may hear, Bleak House girl is a servant

indicators.note: this phrase means the word is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: Ada Clare is a ward in Dickens's novel Bleak House

explanation.surface: A Dickens heroine said to be a servant.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent Ada and the answer sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: An aider is a helper, one who serves or assists.

clue.text: Imported from Taiwan? Unlikely

definitions.meaning: literally brought from a distant place

explanation.surface: Goods brought in from Taiwan dismissed as improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: Far-fetched means improbable or hard to believe, and literally brought from afar.

clue.text: Hard left accepts a royal prince

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A hard-line left-winger welcoming a prince.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is the young Henry V in Shakespeare's history plays.
explanation.definitionFit: Prince Hal is the youthful nickname of Henry V in Shakespeare.

clue.text: Resort with no end of poor-quality accommodation

indicators.note: with no end of means the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a hovel is a squalid dwelling

explanation.surface: A seaside town whose lodgings are shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: HOVE is a seaside resort beside Brighton on the English south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: Hove is an English seaside resort in East Sussex.

clue.text: Female was distressed, locked in tower

indicators.note: locked in means shut inside, so the rearranged letters go within the female word

parts.note: her refers to a female

indicators.note: distressed means upset, so the letters of was are scrambled

explanation.surface: A distraught princess imprisoned in a tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distressed' makes AWS, which 'locked in' places inside the female pronoun. 'tower' is something that tows, not a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawser is a thick rope used for towing ships, so a tower in the sense of something that tows.

clue.text: Left meat soaking in fat

indicators.note: soaking in means immersed within, so the meat sits inside the fat

parts.note: lard is pig fat
boar is meat from a wild pig

explanation.surface: A joint of meat steeping in fat.
explanation.walkthrough: LARBOARD is the old nautical term for the left side of a ship, now port.
explanation.definitionFit: Larboard is the old nautical word for port, the left side of a vessel.
